blazers.pulse: The hot start cooled off with two straight losses, and Portland sits at 6-3. Luka Doncic dropped 53 on them in LA on Friday, then Wembanyama's Spurs ran them off the floor the next night, reopening old wounds from last spring's playoff exit.
storylines: Lost 125-103 to the Spurs on Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back: Wembanyama had 29 in 24 minutes and Avdija led Portland with just 15.
Blazers broadcasters ripped Wembanyama for flopping, but both teams shot 33 free throws, so the officiating excuse doesn't really hold up.
Lost 124-118 at the Lakers on Friday in an NBA Cup game as Doncic scored a league-high 53; Avdija (22 pts, 11 ast, 9 reb) and Lillard (22) kept it close.
Yahoo's takeaways say the schedule is an easy excuse, but Portland was simply outplayed on both ends by San Antonio, the team that bounced them in five games last spring.

timbers.pulse: Mission accomplished: Portland won 2-0 at Austin on Decision Day to finish seventh and skip the Wild Card. Four straight wins to close the season has fans feeling like this team is peaking at the right time.
storylines: Beat Austin 2-0 on Saturday: Ariel Lassiter scored in the 3rd minute, Kristoffer Velde added one in the 70th, and James Pantemis made seven saves.
Finished 13-14-7 with 46 points, the No. 7 seed in the West, after winning the last four games of the season.
Round One is a best-of-three against No. 2 FC Dallas; Game 2 is at Providence Park on Nov. 28.
Pantemis: 'We've been in playoff mode for the last three to four weeks.' Dallas coach Eric Quill called Portland's home ground probably the hardest place to play in the league.

f1.pulse: Lando Norris won a wet, chaotic São Paulo GP, but the talk is Max Verstappen charging from 21st on the grid to second. Mercedes wrapped up the constructors' title, so both 2026 championships are now settled with three races left.
storylines: Podium: Norris, Verstappen, Isack Hadjar, giving Red Bull a double podium; Russell 4th and champion Antonelli 5th.
Mercedes clinched the constructors' crown with three races to go, matching Williams' nine titles.
Engine penalties sent Verstappen, Hamilton and Leclerc down the grid; Verstappen blamed a slow start on holding the clutch wrong and thinks a win was possible.
Rough day for Ferrari: Hamilton went from 20th to 9th in his 400th F1 start despite a spin, and Leclerc was 8th with a five-second penalty.
